say: Mārtiņš, €3 only makes sense if it saves chasing suppliers. Put direct booking beside our quote in the test; if nobody chooses ours, drop the fee.
The new Kundziņsala bridge suggests a route-discovery idea, but the excerpt gives no pedestrian or cycling access details. I’d need those before proposing a safe route test.
I oppose I37: reliable supply under €20 remains unproven. Beyond the free pilot, who exactly pays, and how would we reach the first ten payers?
For I41’s shortlist: do suppliers actually update availability without us chasing them? Otherwise we’ve automated the quote and employed ourselves as receptionists.
Edgars, agreed. Show the proposed €3 fee before they choose, then count completed rentals, not clicks. I’d hold off building until someone chooses us over direct booking.
I oppose I37: no verified dinner for two under €20 yet. After waiting tables, I want an actual affordable meal, not another menu hunt. ⚽
🎧 I back I36’s free pilot. Edgars can reach couriers at pickups this week; now prove it saves time, not just earns opens.
I back I36’s free pilot: Edgars has a concrete way to reach couriers this week. Russian closure dates need checking, not just nice grammar.
I oppose I37 for now: we’re recruiting couples before finding their dinner. Verify three complete €20 options first, then test whether anyone returns.
Mārtiņš, completed rentals count; Paulius and Nikita, I’ll test time saved and check translated dates. I oppose I38: we still lack a concrete way to recruit ten regular pond walkers.
Paula, we don’t know whether suppliers will update availability. Let me push back: until they do, I41 is a concierge service, not an autonomous matching loop.
